resources.string: Record and play back every source, live level
The audio service is missing: audioserver is not running or crashed at boot.
The audio policy exposes no input: the primary HAL declares no input devices (check the devicePorts of type AUDIO_DEVICE_IN in audio_policy_configuration.xml).
No BUILTIN_MIC input: the built-in microphone port is missing from the audio policy.
The microphone is muted system-wide (isMicrophoneMute): every recording will be silent.
getMicrophones() is empty: the audio HAL does not implement microphone characteristics (common on old HALs, only informative).
The HAL returned an error for the microphone characteristics.
Skipped: UNPROCESSED is not declared by the device
No NS, AGC or AEC (%1$d effects in total)
No acoustic echo canceller: VoIP and VoLTE calls rely on the modem/ADSP echo cancellation, if any.
The audio policy found no input profile for this source and format: check the input mixPorts in audio_policy_configuration.xml, or the HAL failed open_input_stream.
The input could not start: another app holds the microphone, or the HAL failed to start the input stream (pcm_open of the capture device).
read() returned no samples: the input HAL is not delivering data (capture pcm blocked, ADSP or SLIMbus/MI2S port not running).
Silence: capture silenced by the system
Android silenced this capture (app in background, microphone privacy toggle, or another app with priority is recording). Repeat with the app in front.
Digital silence: every sample is exactly zero
The input path delivers zeros: mixer path closed, wrong ADC route, or codec/mic bias not powered. Check mixer_paths*.xml for this capture device and the codec in logcat.
Constant value: the samples never change
A constant non-zero value means a stuck ADC or a wrong data format (bit width / slot mapping) on the capture port.
Near silence (RMS %1$s dBFS): only the lowest bits move, the analog gain or the mic bias is probably off.
%1$s %% of the samples are clipped in a normal room: the capture gain is too high.
DC offset of %1$s %%: mic bias or the ADC high-pass filter is wrong.
Very loud for ambient noise (RMS %1$s dBFS): excessive gain, hum or a noisy capture path.
Data arrives at %1$d frames/s instead of %2$d: the input stream is slower than real time.
The first samples arrived after %1$d ms: slow input start in the HAL.
Recorded from %1$s instead of %2$s: the audio policy ignored the preferred device.
Stereo capture was refused, recorded in mono.
Left and right channels are identical: one microphone is duplicated on both channels.
Used by the live meter and by the recording
Ambient noise is enough: no need to speak
Digital silence for %1$d s: the capture path delivers only zeros.
Speak a few words, then listen on the speaker or the earpiece
Choose a duration and record: the result appears here with its levels.
The recording from %1$s sounds clear: voice intelligible, no hum, hiss or distortion.
%1$d audio effects declared by the ROM
